Today, there is no limit on how long councilmembers can serve on the City Council .
This measure limits Council members to three consecutive four-year terms, twelve years of
service, after which they must step away for two years before seeking a seat again. It is not
a ban. It is a pause that reopens every seat to the community.
Term limits bring new voices, new ideas, and new energy into City Hall. They widen the path
for residents who have never seen a realistic opening to run. They ensure that experience is
renewed rather than merely accumulated, and that our government reflects the East Palo
is written to be fair. It applies going forward only. No current Council member's
past service is counted against them, and no one is removed from a seat they hold today.
Six Cities across San Mateo County already have term limits. The San Mateo County Board
of Supervisors is limited to three terms and twelve years, exactly what this measure asks of
us, The legislators who represent us in Sacramento, the Governor, and the President are all
Twelve years is a full and generous opportunity to serve. After that, our neighbors deserve a
real chance to choose someone new, and the best ideas should have to earn support all
is a vote for accountability, for competition, and for a City Council
that stays close to the people it serves.
